title: AlphaTensor discovers faster matrix multiplication algorithms over GF(2), immediately built upon by independent mathematicians
summary: AlphaTensor found a 47-multiplication 4x4 scheme over GF(2) and a 96 for 5x5; Kauers and Moosbauer improved the latter to 95.
account: On 5 October 2022 Nature published AlphaTensor, a reinforcement-learning system from DeepMind (Fawzi, Balog, Huang, Hubert, Romera-Paredes and others) that treats the search for matrix multiplication algorithms as a single-player game, TensorGame, in which a deep neural network guides a planning procedure derived from AlphaZero. It found an algorithm multiplying two 4x4 matrices over the field with two elements in 47 multiplications, beating Strassen's two-level algorithm for the first time in about 50 years, and a 96-multiplication scheme for 5x5 matrices over the same field. On 8 October 2022 Manuel Kauers and Jakob Moosbauer posted a preprint, revised on 13 October, that took the published 5x5 scheme as its starting point and improved it to 95 multiplications.
purpose: Built to discover matrix multiplication algorithms by searching for low-rank tensor decompositions; the new schemes were that purpose.
system: AlphaTensor (AlphaZero-derived reinforcement learning for tensor decomposition)

ratings.reason: Researchers in algebraic complexity gained new explicit decompositions that were improved upon within a week by Kauers and Moosbauer; the gains are field-restricted, since Nature reports the 4x4 improvement for matrices “in a finite field” and Kauers and Moosbauer give the 5x5 record of 96 multiplications over Z2.

ai_role.statement: The reinforcement-learning agent found the decompositions, which are explicit and checkable; the independent preprint treats the 96-multiplication 5x5 result as established and improves it, which corroborates the result's existence. The 47-multiplication 4x4 scheme rests on the vendor paper's published decomposition.

evidence.citation: Fawzi, A. et al. (2022). Discovering faster matrix multiplication algorithms with reinforcement learning. Nature 610, 47–53.
evidence.title: Discovering faster matrix multiplication algorithms with reinforcement learning
evidence.quote: Particularly relevant is the case of 4 × 4 matrices in a finite field, where AlphaTensor's algorithm improves on Strassen's two-level algorithm for the first time, to our knowledge, since its discovery 50 years ago.

evidence.citation: Kauers, M. and Moosbauer, J. (2022). The FBHHRBNRSSSHK-Algorithm for Multiplication in Z2^(5x5) is still not the end of the story. arXiv:2210.04045.
evidence.title: The FBHHRBNRSSSHK-Algorithm for Multiplication in Z2^(5x5) is still not the end of the story
evidence.quote: In response to a recent Nature article which announced an algorithm for multiplying 5×5-matrices over ℤ₂ with only 96 multiplications, two fewer than the previous record

produced_by: Formulation of algorithm discovery as a tensor-decomposition game
Neural-network-guided search with exact verification of each decomposition
Publication of explicit decompositions that others can check and extend
must_hold: Decompositions must be verified exactly over the stated ring or field
Independent reproduction or extension by researchers outside the vendor

echoes.setting: AlphaEvolve (Google DeepMind) found a scheme multiplying 4x4 complex-valued matrices in 48 scalar multiplications; Dumas, Pernet and Sedoglavic (arXiv:2506.13242, submitted 16 June 2025) derived a 48-multiplication scheme with rational coefficients from AlphaEvolve's complex-valued decomposition, valid over any ring except characteristic 2

headline: AlphaTensor finds a 47-multiplication 4x4 scheme over GF(2)
metric: multiplying two 4x4 matrices over the field with two elements in 47 multiplications

later.note: Three days after publication, Kauers and Moosbauer took AlphaTensor's 96-multiplication 5x5 scheme over Z2 as a starting point and improved it to 95, confirming and extending the result.
later.quote: In response to a recent Nature article which announced an algorithm for multiplying 5×5-matrices over ℤ2 with only 96 multiplications, two fewer than the previous record, we present an algorithm that does the job with only 95 multiplications.

claim_basis: One independent preprint and the makers' peer-reviewed study are on file. There is no independent study or report and no finding by a regulator or court.
